def: Foreign matter or off-grade material mixed into a food commodity, measured as a percentage of the total lot.
Payment made by the buyer before goods are shipped, often as a percentage of order value with the balance due later.
A toxin produced by certain moulds that can occur in grains, pulses, nuts and spices; many markets set maximum allowable limits.
Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority — the Indian government body registering and supporting agricultural exporters.
A document issued by the shipping line acknowledging receipt of cargo and serving as a contract of carriage and title document.
Cargo shipped loose (not in containers or packages), such as grain loaded directly into a vessel's hold.
A payment method where the buyer pays upon presentation of shipping documents, typically through the banks involved.
A document certifying the country in which goods were produced, often required for customs clearance or preferential tariff treatment.
An Incoterm where the seller pays for transport to the destination port; risk transfers to the buyer once goods are loaded at origin.
An Incoterm where the seller pays for transport and insurance to the destination port; risk transfers once goods are loaded at origin.
A document itemising the goods sold, their value and terms of sale, used for customs valuation.
The party named to receive a shipment, typically the buyer or their agent.
A facility where containers are stored, loaded and unloaded before or after ocean transport.
A charge levied when a container is not returned or picked up within the free time allowed by the shipping line or port.
Directorate General of Foreign Trade — the Indian government body regulating and licensing foreign trade, including export policy.
A standard shipping container without temperature control, used for non-perishable dry cargo.
A company whose core business is exporting goods, often across multiple product categories, as distinct from a manufacturer that exports occasionally.
An Incoterm where the seller makes goods available at their premises; the buyer arranges and bears the cost/risk of all transport from there.
A shipment that fills an entire container, booked and billed as a single unit.
A document certifying that cargo or packaging (often wooden pallets) has been treated against pests, often required for phytosanitary compliance.
An Incoterm where the seller delivers goods loaded onto the vessel at the origin port; risk transfers to the buyer at that point.
A company that arranges shipping logistics on behalf of an importer or exporter, including booking carriers and handling documentation.
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India — India's domestic food safety regulator (not an export certification body).
Global Agricultural Information Network report — USDA Foreign Agricultural Service country-level agricultural trade reports.
The classification of a commodity by quality criteria such as size, colour, moisture or defect percentage.
Goods and Services Tax — India's domestic indirect tax; exports are generally zero-rated under Indian GST law.
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points — a food-safety management system methodology used in some processing facilities.
A document certifying that a food product (commonly seafood or meat) meets the health/sanitary standards of the destination market.
An internationally standardised numerical classification for traded products, used for customs and tariff purposes.
The registration number issued by India's DGFT that a business must hold to legally export from or import into India.
A set of standardised international trade terms (published by the ICC) defining responsibilities for shipping, insurance and risk between buyer and seller.
A freezing method where each piece of product is frozen separately rather than as a solid block, common for seafood.
India's 8-digit extension of the international HS code, used for Indian customs and export policy classification.
A large flexible bulk container, typically holding 500kg–1.5 tonnes, used for grains, feed and fertilizer.
A shipment that doesn't fill a full container and is consolidated with other shippers' cargo.
A bank-issued payment guarantee to the seller, conditional on presentation of compliant shipping documents.
A specific batch of product with a shared origin, harvest/production date and quality characteristics.
An outer shipping carton containing multiple retail or inner units, typically used for packaged/frozen goods.
A government-set floor price below which a product cannot legally be exported, sometimes used to manage domestic supply.
A ventilated net bag used for some fresh produce to allow airflow during transit.
The percentage of water in a commodity, a key specification for grains, pulses, spices and dried products affecting shelf life and weight.
The smallest quantity a supplier is willing to sell in a single order.
Marine Products Export Development Authority — the Indian government body overseeing seafood exports.
A document detailing the contents, weights and dimensions of each package in a shipment.
A document certifying that plant-origin goods are free from pests and diseases, issued by the exporting country's plant protection authority.
A quality check performed on goods before they are loaded for export, to verify they meet the agreed specification.
A refrigerated shipping container used to transport temperature-sensitive cargo such as fresh produce or frozen seafood.
A certificate issued by an export promotion body (such as APEDA) confirming an exporter's registration for a product category.
The company that owns or operates the vessel transporting containerised or bulk cargo.
The agreed set of measurable quality criteria for a product order — grade, size, moisture, admixture, etc.
A direct electronic bank transfer used as a payment method in international trade.
The time a shipment takes to travel from origin port to destination port.
The process of unloading cargo at an intermediate port and reloading it onto another vessel en route to its final destination.
Estimated Time of Arrival / Estimated Time of Departure for a shipping vessel.
The international body that maintains and updates the Harmonized System (HS) classification used globally for customs purposes.
A lab report confirming a product's measured characteristics (e.g. moisture, purity, residue levels) against a specification.
The country where goods were produced or manufactured, which must be declared for customs and labelling purposes.
A licensed professional who handles import/export customs clearance on behalf of a buyer or seller.
A tax imposed by the importing country's government on goods entering its territory, usually based on HS classification and value.
A treaty between countries reducing or eliminating tariffs on trade between them.
The total cost of a shipment once it has arrived at the buyer's destination, including product cost, freight, insurance, duties and local charges.
How much product weight or volume fits within a given container or package format.
The reservation of container/cargo space on a specific ship's sailing, arranged with a shipping line or forwarder.
